title: Contrastive-ranking rubric and multi-judge temperature harmonization for config rollouts
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Create a new contrastive-ranking rubric and a multi-judge LLM adjudication pattern with temperature harmonization and per-cohort calibration to reduce false-positive regressions caused by config or model variant changes. Integrate gating signals into the rollout pipeline so config/model rollouts are automatically flagged or blocked when calibrated cohort deltas exceed thresholds.
background: Current eval pipelines use absolute score rubrics and single-judge LLM-as-judge settings which are brittle to config-level changes (batching, quantization, temperature) and cohort shifts. This leads to noisy regression signals during model/config rollouts and frequent manual adjudication. We need a scoring methodology that: (1) focuses on relative ranking/contrastive comparisons instead of absolute scalar scores, (2) ensembles judge outputs across temperature settings and model variants to reduce judgement bias, and (3) produces per-cohort calibration factors so thresholds are comparable across workloads.
proposed_solution:
1) Define a contrastive-ranking rubric: replace many absolute thresholds with pairwise comparisons and margin-based scoring for categories (correctness, hallucination, style fidelity).
2) Implement multi-judge ensemble in eval harness: run 3 judge instances per sample at varied temperatures (e.g., 0.0, 0.3, 0.7) and aggregate via consensus weighting and rank aggregation (Borda or Copeland).
3) Add temperature harmonization: learn small per-temperature scaling factors so different temperatures map to a common score distribution for judge outputs.
4) Per-cohort calibration: compute calibration curves per cohort (prompt type, length bucket, user locale) and store cohort-level offsets used when comparing rollouts.
5) Integrate gating: add pass/fail criteria to rollout pipeline using calibrated effect sizes and a minimum sample size rule; provide manual override with audit trail.
6) Create migration plan and docs: guidance for converting existing rubrics and historical baseline recomputation for last 6 months of evals.
acceptance_criteria: Contrastive-ranking rubric document published in Confluence with examples and conversion guidelines
Eval harness PR merged that supports multi-judge runs and outputs per-sample rank aggregations (unit tests + integration tests)
Temperature harmonization routine implemented and validated on 3 benchmark cohorts with before/after distribution plots
Per-cohort calibration tables generated for at least 5 production cohorts and stored in eval metadata store
Rollout gating rule implemented: rollouts auto-block when calibrated cohort effect size > 0.15 (or configurable) and sample size >= 200
Dashboard shows new metrics (calibrated delta, consensus variance, false-regression rate) and alerting configured
Runbook updated and at least one canary rollout run completed with documented outcome
metrics: Calibrated delta: mean change in contrastive-rank score per cohort
Consensus variance: variance across judge temperatures per sample
False-regression rate: percent of blocked rollouts that post-hoc were deemed non-regressions after adjudication
Sensitivity: true positive detection rate on synthetic regressions injected during validation
Eval throughput: wall-clock time per 1k samples for multi-judge ensemble
Sample requirement: proportion of cohorts meeting N>=200 samples
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): Publish rubric + prototype eval harness support behind feature flag; run on historical datasets only
Phase 2 (week 3): Run multi-judge ensemble on three production cohorts in read-only mode and generate calibration tables; produce dashboards
Phase 3 (week 4): Enable gating in canary rollouts for a single internal customer with manual approvals required
Phase 4 (week 5-6): Gradually expand gating to more internal rollouts and then to external low-traffic customers; default thresholds may be tuned
Rollback path: disable gating flag or revert to single-judge baseline; run incident playbook for false blocks
test_plan: Unit tests for rank aggregation and temperature scaling functions
Integration test that runs full multi-judge eval on a 1k-sample synthetic dataset and verifies consensus stats
Synthetic regression experiments: inject controlled degradations and verify calibrated delta detects >90% with <10% false positives
End-to-end canary with monitored dashboard and post-canary manual adjudication summary
Regression coverage to ensure change does not break existing eval export schemas
